hints.title: Modular Exponentiation Decomposition
hints.text: The large exponent array represents a number in base 10. Notice that a^(10x + d) equals (a^x)^10 * a^d modulo 1337.

hints.title: Right-to-Left Exponent Reduction
hints.text: Pop the last digit d of array b. Recurse or iterate: superPow(a, b[:-1])^10 * a^d % 1337.

hints.title: Binary Exponentiation Helper
hints.text: Implement pow_mod(base, exp, 1337) using logarithmic binary exponentiation to quickly evaluate power of 10 and power of d.

hints.title: See the blueprint

variables: N: length of exponent array b
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Reconstructing the full integer exponent from array b causes big integer overflow or extreme slowdown.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Horner method of polynomial evaluation in base 10 keeps intermediate results bounded modulo 1337.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should apply modular arithmetic properties: (x * y) % m = ((x % m) * (y % m)) % m.
